key_insight: A causal dilated CNN can detect radiation-induced charge jumps in superconducting qubits fast enough for real-time, in-the-loop control.
engineering_relevance: The method is FPGA-deployable on QICK/ZCU216 with microsecond latency, making charge-jump detection a practical control primitive for quantum hardware.
method: Train on synthetic Ramsey tomography scans derived from measured qubit templates.
Use a dilated causal convolutional neural network for online inference.
Translate to FPGA firmware with hls4ml using ap_fixed<16,6> quantization.
evidence_signal: At matched false-positive rate, the DCCNN achieved detection efficiency comparable to the offline chi-squared baseline (0.843 ± 0.022 vs. 0.866 ± 0.020) on |Δq| ∈ [0.1, 0.5] e, with 6.19 μs per-inference latency.
watch_item: Performance was trained on synthetic scans and depends on quantization/FPGA deployment details, so robustness to unseen qubit drift and experimental noise should be validated.
paper_title: Real-Time Detection of Charge Jumps in Superconducting Qubits with a Convolutional Neural Network
